title.narrative: Promotion of Solar Tuk Tuk for Public Transportation for Rural in Gedaref State

description.narrative: In rural Gedaref State, Sudan, transportation for people and agricultural goods relies on outdated petrol-powered three-wheelers and donkey carts, which are inefficient, costly, and environmentally harmful. Rising fuel prices and unreliable petrol availability make it difficult for farmers to access markets, often rendering trade unprofitable and limiting local economic growth. These challenges constrain value chains, increase post-harvest losses, and deepen rural poverty while contributing to environmental degradation through fossil fuel dependence.This project addresses these challenges by introducing solar-powered Tuk Tuks supported by community-based solar charging hubs to create an affordable, sustainable, and reliable transportation system. By replacing petrol-powered vehicles with solar alternatives, the project will enhance market access for farmers, reduce transportation costs, and generate new income opportunities for men and women through gender-responsive ownership and capacity-building programs. The solar charging hubs will also serve broader community energy needs, fostering resilience and self-sufficiency. By demonstrating the commercial viability of green transportation solutions, the project encourages private sector participation and presents a scalable model for clean rural mobility, advancing livelihoods, environmental sustainability, and inclusive economic growth.
